issues.description: The template defines a function named create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate in tensor_networks.py, but the problem statement and the solution expect a function named create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate. This name mismatch is structural: students following the problem text or the reference solution will look for create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate but the template provides a differently named entrypoint, which will cause confusion and make it unclear which function to implement or test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate (or add a wrapper function with the expected name that calls the existing implementation). Update the template docstring to match the problem statement naming to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The tensor-network two-qubit gate factory is referred to as create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate in the problem statement and in the solution, but the template defines this function as create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual API (creating a nearest-neighbor / adjacent two-qubit gate tensor) can confuse students when they search for the function to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent name across all artifacts. Either rename the template function create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate to create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate, or update the problem statement and solution to use create_adjacent_two_qubit_gate. Prefer matching the problem statement (create_nearest_neighbor_two_qubit_gate) so students clearly see the task name and template stub align.
